From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>

Date: 2027-08-16T14:22:00Z
Subject: Re: Redwood adapter interop & test plan

+1 to the proposed schedule. A few technical questions to prep the deep-dive so we avoid surprises:

1) Model & token semantics
- Which model variants will you call? (e.g., open-llama-7B, Llama2-13B or your in-house distilled variant)
- Typical sequence lengths and distribution (prompt vs completion lengths) — helps us size KV cache and batch configs.

2) Streaming & function-calling
- Do you use chunked server-sent events or WebSocket streaming? Any special framing?
- Examples of the function call payloads and expected callback/confirmation pattern.

3) Authentication & connectivity
- Are you using mTLS, API-key, or federated OIDC for non-prod endpoints?
- Any CIDR ranges for egress allowlisting (we can provide our outbound IP list for the sandbox pool).

4) Observability & failure modes
- For the scaled smoke, please provide the failure tolerance (e.g., 95th pct latency SLO) and desired observability artifacts (traces, raw request logs, token-level costs).

5) Test artifacts
- If you can drop a small sample payload (<=1MB) and a redacted function schema into the Drive folder that would be ideal.

I'll prepare a short runbook covering the endpoints/headers we expect, a canonical sample curl + websocket snippet, and a minimal load profile.

Cheers,
Jonas Weber
Senior Runtime Engineer | Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.ai

--
From: Elena Rossi <elena@zekon.consulting>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: eng@zekon.consulting, Tonio Marquez <tonio.marquez@zekon.consulting>
Date: 2027-08-17T08:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Redwood adapter interop & test plan

Thanks Jonas — answers inline below (quoting your questions):

> 1) Model & token semantics
We plan to call three variants during tests: open-llama-7B-quant, zoptera-inhouse-6B (distilled), and gpt-compat-2-13B for a performance baseline. Typical prompts average 220 tokens, completions around 160 tokens; 95th percentile completion length ~800 tokens for a small subset (long-form generation).

> 2) Streaming & function-calling
We stream over WebSocket with newline-delimited JSON chunks (frame per partial delta); function calls are declared via a schema and we expect a single JSON object returned to the client. We'll upload a redacted sample payload to Drive: test-window-sample-payload.json (no PII).

> 3) Authentication & connectivity
Non-prod uses API-keys for now; we can switch to mTLS if required for the EU sandbox. For allowlist: our egress is dynamic but we can provide an ASN and IP ranges (we'll add these to the Drive folder).

> 4) Observability & failure modes
Target SLO for the smoke test: 99th percentile latency < 2.5s for the short-call profile; for the long-form subset we'll accept higher tails but want to capture traces. We'll share structured failure repros if we hit degradation.

> 5) Test artifacts
Uploaded: test-window-sample-payload.json, function-schema-redacted.json. Also dropped the IP ranges file.

Attachments (uploaded to Drive): test-window-sample-payload.json; function-schema-redacted.json
